record_type_quote: Therefore, the present study conducted a high-power replication of Yoshida et al. using a lexicality maze task with 324 participants and 24 sets of materials.

targets.authors: Yoshida M, Dickey MW, Sturt P
targets.title: Predictive processing of syntactic structure: sluicing and ellipsis in real-time sentence processing.
targets.outcome_quote: The experiment revealed gender mismatch effects at the reflexive, which crucially did not interact with wh-type. The absence of the wh-type by gender interaction suggests that, at the wh-phrase, the parser constructs the entire wh-clause with its subject NP coindexed with the first clause subject NP, irrespective of the type of wh-phrase. This finding is partially inconsistent with Yoshida et al., who observed gender mismatch effects only in the wh-NP conditions.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit partial inconsistency: predictive processing and wh-NP mismatch effect agree, but mismatch in wh-PP and garden-path effects differ from the original.
